headlines.text: On this day in 2023, the AEW TNT Title had a new owner by the end of the night as Darby Allin vs. Samoa Joe battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.66 ? a good, competitive contest ? ending the champion's reign at 9 defenses. Allin attacked Joe with a skateboard and a ladder before the bell even rang, then capped a hometown title win with back-to-back Coffin Drops as Sting embraced him in an emotional moment.
Turning the clock back to 2025: Brian Cage vs. Dante Martin vs. Komander vs. The Beast Mortos settled things in a High Speed Collision match on Collision, rated 6.22.

Flash back to 2023, when The Acclaimed vs. Jarrett & Lethal went to battle over the AEW World Tag Team Titles, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.56. It was the first title opportunity of Jarrett & Lethal's career. This stood as the 50th match in AEW World Tag Team Titles history ? a real piece of championship history. It marked The Acclaimed's 10th match with the title on the line. In a No Holds Barred match, The Acclaimed fought off Jeff Jarrett and Jay Lethal ? with Billy Gunn getting ejected at ringside ? to retain the AEW World Tag Team Championship.

secondaries.text: 2025 brought us this moment: the AEW TNT Title was up for grabs as Daniel Garcia vs. Mark Briscoe went to war, appearing on Collision, rated 7.30 ? a strong outing.
Looking back to 2025, when Rated FTR vs. The Learning Tree (Trio) headlined Collision, rated 6.44 in a wild trios sprint.
Rewind to 2023, when it was the first-ever encounter between Ricky Starks and Chris Jericho, setting the tone as the night's opener on Dynamite, rated 7.31 ? a strong outing.
